title: The Hormuz Illusion — Trump's Friendly Talks vs. the Empty Waterway
narrative: President Trump, speaking at a Michigan rally and aboard Air Force One on July 27-28, described 'very friendly negotiations' with Iran, claiming 'I think there's a good chance that something could happen.' He told the GM crowd that Iran is 'pleading' with the U.S. to end the naval blockade: 'Please, please, no blockade.' Trump also claimed he paused strikes because 'all of the people that deal with Iran asked me: Don't fire.' UN Ambassador Mike Waltz said the president is 'giving diplomacy some space.' Markets rallied — Brent crude fell ~$9 to $98/barrel — on hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough.
telemetry: MarineTraffic AIS data (July 24-26): Only 29 vessels crossed Hormuz in THREE DAYS — 21 exiting, 8 entering; pre-war baseline: 88-153/day (~90% collapse)

Hormuzmonitor.com: daily transits fallen to single digits for non-Iranian ships; Iran running 'selective blockade' — India, China, Pakistan, Turkey allowed case-by-case; US/allied vessels blocked entirely
CENTCOM (July 27): US naval forces redirected 17 commercial vessels, disabled 2, boarded 2 — blockade 'remains in full effect'
Iran's foreign ministry explicitly denied ANY negotiations: spokesman Baghaei called reports of talks 'fabricated' and said 'This is not in our DNA'
During the 'ceasefire': Saudi Arabia intercepted drones; Jordan shot down 3 drones in 48 hours; Houthis claimed strikes on Yanbu port; drones hit Erbil targeting US consulate
Shipping reality: war risk insurance cancelled since March 5; Maersk, MSC, Hapag-Lloyd, CMA CGM all suspended Hormuz transits
June interim deal collapsed precisely because of ambiguous language about who controls Hormuz — the same issue remains unresolved
analysis:
The Hormuz data tells the real story, and it is brutal. Twenty-nine vessels crossed the strait in three days — a 90% collapse from the pre-war baseline. The US naval blockade continues: 17 vessels redirected, 2 disabled, 2 boarded. Iran explicitly denies any negotiations whatsoever, calling the reports 'fabricated.' The shipping industry has voted with its hulls — every major carrier has suspended transits, and war-risk insurance has been cancelled since March.

Trump's narrative — Iran 'pleading' to end the blockade, 'friendly negotiations,' a 'good chance' of a deal — is constructed for an audience of two: oil markets and American voters. Markets responded exactly as designed, with Brent falling ~$9 on peace hopes. But the underlying reality hasn't changed: the strait is functionally closed to global commerce, the blockade continues, and Iran denies any diplomatic channel exists beyond intermediaries.

The drone attacks that continued during the 'ceasefire' confirm the kinetic reality. Saudi Arabia shot down drones Monday. Jordan shot down three in 48 hours. The Houthis claimed strikes on Yanbu. Drones hit Erbil targeting the US consulate area. A ceasefire in which one side stops its airstrikes but everyone else keeps fighting is not a ceasefire. It is a unilateral US operational pause that no other party recognizes.
verdict: [SIPHONED VERDICT]: Trump says Iran is 'pleading' to end the blockade as 'friendly negotiations' progress. MarineTraffic data: 29 vessels in three days — a 90% collapse. Iran denies any talks exist. The blockade continues. Drones still fly. The markets bought the narrative; the waterway didn't.
